title: Anderson Household Task Management
summary: A requirements analysis and prototype for a web application to manage schedules, tasks, invoices, and meals for the Anderson household — replacing a disorganized mix of paper notes and online tools.
problem: The Anderson household's au pair managed everything manually — cooking schedules, bill payments, task delegation — across a fragmented mix of paper notes and unrelated apps. Multiple users with different roles needed to access and update shared information without stepping on each other's changes. The existing approach caused confusion, missed tasks, and an unnecessarily heavy workload.
approach: Led a team of 5 through a full requirements analysis cycle: stakeholder interviews, use-case modeling, functional and non-functional requirements capture, and prototype development. Produced a UML use-case diagram mapping actors (Family, Employee, Au Pair, Grandson, Staff) to system functions. Built interactive wireframes in Figma covering the calendar, to-do list, invoice management, and meal planning modules. Applied MoSCoW prioritization to scope the MVP against a fixed academic deadline.
outcome: Delivered a fully documented requirements specification and a clickable Figma prototype that met all client expectations. The prototype demonstrated how a single central system could reduce the au pair's administrative workload by consolidating five separate tools into one. Received highest marks in the Requirements Analysis course module.
highlights: UML use-case diagram with 5 actor types and 12 system functions
Figma prototype: calendar, to-do list, invoice, and meal modules
Team lead: coordinated 5 members across analysis and design phases
Non-functional requirements: usability, security, performance, reliability

title: Rail Track Anomaly Detection
summary: A two-stage AI workflow segmenting regions of interest and flagging anomalies to support rail maintenance planning.
problem: Manual rail inspection is labor-intensive and inconsistent, and subtle track defects can go unnoticed until they become safety risks.
approach: Designed a two-stage pipeline as part of a team project: a U-Net model segments regions of interest along the track, then a CNN/YOLOv8 stage flags likely anomalies within those regions for review.
outcome: Delivered a working anomaly-flagging pipeline that demonstrates how computer vision can support maintenance planning and reduce reliance on manual visual inspection.

title: Airbnb Data Analysis
summary: A BI project exploring market dynamics and community impact across Antwerp, Brussels, and Ghent.
problem: Understanding Airbnb's market dynamics and community impact across three Belgian cities required consolidating scattered, inconsistent listing and booking data.
approach: Built an ETL pipeline to clean and merge listing data, then designed Qlik Sense dashboards comparing pricing, availability, and neighborhood-level density across Antwerp, Brussels, and Ghent.
outcome: Delivered a BI dashboard that surfaced city-level market and community trends, supporting clearer discussion of short-term rental impact.
highlights: ETL pipeline for multi-city listing data

images.caption: Qlik Sense dashboard — pricing and density by city

title: Image Classification of Rose Species
summary: A computer vision pipeline classifying seven rose species with transfer learning, shipped as a lightweight demo app.
problem: Manually identifying rose species from photos is slow and requires botanical expertise most people don't have.
approach: Built a transfer-learning image classifier over seven rose species using fastai/PyTorch on a curated, augmented dataset, then wrapped it in a Streamlit demo for quick, interactive testing.
outcome: Delivered a working demo achieving strong classification accuracy across species, showing how transfer learning shortens the path from dataset to usable tool.
highlights: Transfer learning on a pretrained CNN

title: AI Builder for Expense Notes
summary: An automation flow scanning receipts into structured expense tracking, simplifying reimbursements and reporting.
problem: Employees manually re-typed receipt data into spreadsheets for reimbursement, which was slow and error-prone.
approach: Built an AI Builder automation flow to scan and extract receipt fields automatically, feeding structured data into a Power BI reporting layer.
outcome: Simplified reimbursement submission and reporting by removing manual data entry from the process.

title: Airport Flight Data Analysis
summary: Exploratory dashboards surfacing delay patterns across airlines, routes, and time windows.
problem: Airlines and analysts lacked a quick way to see delay patterns across routes, carriers, and time windows.
approach: Built exploratory Qlik Sense dashboards breaking down delays by airline, route, and time window for fast comparison.
outcome: Delivered dashboards that made delay patterns visible at a glance, supporting faster root-cause discussion.

title: Job Application Training Assistant
summary: A platform organizing mock interviews at scale, reducing admin effort between students, coordinators, and recruiters.
problem: Coordinating mock interviews between students, coordinators, and recruiters involved heavy manual scheduling and admin work.
approach: Built a Laravel/MySQL platform to schedule, track, and manage mock interview sessions at scale, replacing manual coordination.
outcome: Delivered a live platform that cut scheduling admin time and gave coordinators a single system to manage sessions end-to-end.
highlights: Role-based access for students, coordinators, recruiters
